headline: Caleb Durbin Crushes Yankees At Fenway As Connelly Early Shines On The Mound
morning_brew: That's how you start a series against the Bronx Bombers. We needed a performance like this to shake off the stink of that Colorado trip, and the boys delivered a beautiful six to three victory over the Yankees at Fenway Park last night. Connelly Early was absolutely fantastic on the mound, giving us six strong innings, allowing just two runs while striking out nine. He kept their bats off balance all night long, showing the kind of grit we've been begging to see from this rotation. Then Caleb Durbin stepped up in the fifth inning and crushed a tie-breaking two-run home run that nearly cleared the seats.

The bullpen actually held the lead this time, which is a massive relief after the disasters we watched earlier in the week. Greg Weissert, Danny Coulombe, and Garrett Whitlock did their jobs to bridge the gap, and Aroldis Chapman locked down the save in the ninth. Sully from Southie actually called me in the third inning groaning that we're done, but this team proved him wrong and showed some real fight. We're sitting at thirty-three and forty-six, and while the hill is steep, beating New York at Fenway always makes the coffee taste a little sweeter the next morning.

Down in Foxborough, the offseason chatter is shifting across the pond with rumors linking the Patriots to a potential game in Scotland. That'd be wild, though I'm not sure how the locals will handle Sully trying to explain a cover-two defense in a pub. Back home, the national writers are still disrespecting our skill positions, ranking Drake Maye's supporting cast near the bottom of the league. Let them talk, because Drake Maye and Rhamondre Stevenson are going to turn some heads once the real action starts.

news_digest.dans_take: I suppose the Scotland trip would be fun, but let's make sure we can win some games on our own turf first.
